title: Post-deploy anomaly bounty log — week of 2025-11-03
content:
Meeting: Post-deploy anomaly bounty check-in
Date: 2025-11-04 09:30 PT
Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Sofia, Liam, Jia, Olivia (on-call)
Duration: 40m
Context: Last night's release (train-2025-11-03) pushed runtime v3.8.1 with KV cache improvement and a canary ramp to 10% traffic across us-west1/us-east1. Automated rollout paused at 10% due to elevated 5xx on a subset of inference routes. This doc collects live triage notes, bounty-style findings, and action items for follow-up.

Summary of anomalies observed
- Symptom A: Intermittent 502 on /v1/generate for models using prefix-caching. Error spike started ~01:18 UTC and peaked at 01:35 UTC.
  - Canary impact: 9.6% of canary requests saw transient 502s
  - Triaged as: high frequency but short-lived
  - Initial theory: mismatch in cache eviction + kernel selection race after new batching change

- Symptom B: Increased tail latency on long-context requests (>4096 tokens) in us-east1. P95 jumped from 320ms -> 720ms on flagged nodes.
  - Observed correlation with GPU memory pressure metrics and repeated fallback to CPU path for certain quantized kernels
  - Triaged as: medium severity for serving degradation on long-tail workloads

- Symptom C: Metric drift in cost estimator reported by Optimize: tokens-per-request estimate dropped ~12% for a customer cohort (CS reported churn signal). Likely unrelated but flagged for review.

Quick reproduction notes (steps to see issue locally / in staging)
- For 502 repro: replay canary trace set (trace ids listed in linked artifacts). Simulate concurrent requests with small prefix + rapid cache invalidation header set. Observe 502 within 30–90s of hitting the sequence.
- For latency repro: run long-context batch through canary image with synthetic 5k token prompt. Observe memory allocation spikes in nvidia-smi and kernel switching logs in /var/log/serving/runtime.log

Telemetry snippets (from metrics during incident)
- Canary 5xx rate (01:15–01:45 UTC): 4.2% aggregated, peers in prod: 0.04%
- Node GPU mem usage: spike to 92% on affected pod subset (8 instances)
- Fallback count: kernel-fallback->cpu: ~630 events in 30m window

Immediate mitigations applied during call
- Rolled canary back to 0% at 01:50 UTC to stop customer impact (rollback via rollout controller).
- Scoped emergency config: disabled the new continuous-batching heuristic on canary groups (flag: runtime.continuousBatching=false) to test if batching heuristic triggers race condition.
- Throttled long-context traffic routing to dedicated long-tail pool until kernel fallback root cause is understood.

Findings from quick postmortem experiments
- Disabling continuous-batching reduced 502s to background levels in canary within 12 minutes -> strong signal that batching change interacts with cache eviction timing.
- Memory-pressure linked to specific quantized kernel (q8_fast_attention) selection for sequences >4096 when combined with async KV prefetch. Replacing q8_fast_attention with q4fmulti variant in a canary pod eliminated the tail latency but increased avg token CPU cycles (tradeoff).

Decisions made
- Revert continuous-batching heuristic from v3.8.1 in the next patch release (v3.8.2-hotfix) until we can run a deeper deterministic test.
- Run a focused kernel compatibility test matrix across sequence lengths [512, 2048, 4096, 8192] on p4d and a100 to collect deterministic memory/fallback signals. Owner: Jia. Due: 2025-11-10
- Add a canary-specific stress test in CI that exercises cache invalidation + batching concurrently. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2025-11-07

Action items (owner - due - status)
- Priya - prepare hotfix release notes and rollback plan for 3.8.2-hotfix - 2025-11-06 - in_progress
- Jia - kernel compatibility matrix run + writeup - 2025-11-10 - open
- Ethan - add CI canary stress test and synthetic reproduction job - 2025-11-07 - in_progress
- Sofia - coordinate with CS on customer cohort flagged by Optimize (REL-8429) and confirm if tokens-per-request estimate drift correlates to injected canary traffic - 2025-11-06 - open
- Liam - instrument additional debug logs around cache eviction (trace id, key owner, eviction timestamp) behind a sampling flag and deploy to canary only - 2025-11-06 - in_progress
- Olivia (on-call) - follow up on linked Slack thread and escalate any new customer-impacting alerts - Ongoing - monitoring

Unresolved questions / notes for follow-up
- Is there a deterministic ordering where cache eviction + batching start triggers an invalid KV pointer leading to 502, or is it a timing window only observable under load? Need deterministic repro harness.
- Does q8_fast_attention regression happen only under specific memory fragmentation patterns introduced by async prefetch? The kernel team should validate allocator interactions.
- Should we split canary pool by model family to limit blast radius on future kernel experiments? Long-term ops decision.

Risk register (short)
- Risk: Reintroducing batching without full matrix testing could cause customer outages. Mitigation: hold on default until validated. Owner: Priya.
- Risk: Kernel swaps to q4 variants increase CPU cost per token for long-context customers and may affect billing estimates. Mitigation: inform Optimize to run cost projections and notify affected customers. Owner: Sofia.

Communication plan
- Internal: Brief exec on rollback and impact (email + Slack) by EOD 2025-11-04. Owner: Priya.
- Customer-facing: CS templated note for impacted customers explaining rollback and expected stability improvement. Draft by Sofia by 2025-11-06.

Appendix: short raw logs (sanitized)
- [01:19:23 UTC] pod-serving-us-west1-7f4: ERROR runtime: serve failed: cache-key not found after eviction; trace=trace-00a1
- [01:20:12 UTC] pod-serving-us-east1-2b1: WARN runtime: kernel fallback triggered (q8_fast_attention -> cpu) seq_len=5120
- [01:34:02 UTC] rollout-controller: canary throttle: reducing traffic to 0% for train-2025-11-03

Notes to self / scribbles
- Need to add a post-deploy checklist item: run quick canary stress with eviction toggle for every batching-related change.
- Consider an automated canary rollback timer if 5xx>1% sustained for >5m.
- Follow up with kernel team to get prefetch & allocator engineers into the matrix run.

Meeting adjourned 10:10 PT. Next follow-up: Rapid sync 2025-11-06 08:00 PT to review kernel matrix results and decide hotfix publish timing.
